words.ex: The blockade stopped all ships from entering the port.
words.ex_cn: 封锁阻止了所有船只进入港口。
words.en: A blockade is an action to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving a place.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: The old song is reminiscent of my childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌让人想起我的童年。
words.en: If you say that one thing is reminiscent of another, you mean that it reminds you of it.

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.tr: n. 关税；税率；（旅馆、饭店等的）价目表
words.ex: The government raised the tariff on imported cars.
words.ex_cn: 政府提高了进口汽车的关税。
words.en: A tariff is a tax that a government collects on goods coming into a country.

words.ex: The job position is still vacant.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位仍然空缺。
words.en: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.tr:
v. 改造；修整
n. 改组；改建
words.ex: They will revamp the old website next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将改造旧网站。
words.en: To revamp something means to change it in order to improve it or make it more modern.

words.ex: We recycle plastic bottles every week.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周回收塑料瓶。
words.en: To recycle means to process used materials so that they can be used again.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: He walks with a prosthetic leg.
words.ex_cn: 他用假腿走路。
words.en: Prosthetic refers to an artificial device that replaces a missing body part, which may be lost through trauma, disease, or congenital conditions.

words.ex: In this village, it is a custom to light lanterns during the festival.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村庄，节日期间点灯笼是一种习俗。
words.en: A custom is an activity, a way of behaving, or an event which is usual or traditional in a particular society or in particular circumstances.

words.ex: He needs surgery for his broken arm.
words.ex_cn: 他需要做手术来治疗断掉的胳膊。
words.en: Surgery is the medical specialty that uses operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to investigate or treat a pathological condition such as a disease or injury, to help improve bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwanted ruptured areas.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；开玩笑；戏谑
words.ex: He played a prank on his friend with a fake spider.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个假蜘蛛捉弄了他的朋友。
words.en: A prank is a trick or practical joke that is played on someone, often to make them look foolish or to amuse others.

words.ex: He posted an anonymous comment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在网上发布了一条匿名评论。
words.en: If you remain anonymous when you do something, you do not let people know that you were the person who did it.

words.ex: The turtle outlives the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟比兔子活得长。
words.en: To live longer than someone else; to survive something.

words.tr: n. 汇编程序；汇编机；装配工
words.ex: The programmer wrote code for the assembler.
words.ex_cn: 程序员为汇编程序编写了代码。
words.en: An assembler is a type of computer program that interprets software programs written in assembly language into machine language, code, and instructions that can be executed by a computer.

words.tr: adj. 松果体的；松果状的; n. 松果腺；松果体
words.ex: The pineal gland helps control sleep.
words.ex_cn: 松果体帮助调节睡眠。
words.en: Relating to the pineal gland, a small endocrine gland in the brain of vertebrates that produces melatonin.

words.tr: n. 损害；身体上的伤害
words.ex: The doctor found a lesion on his skin.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的皮肤上发现了一个病灶。
words.en: A lesion is an area of damage to the body, such as a wound, ulcer, or tumor.

words.ex: The blind man walks with a white cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位失明的男人用白色手杖走路。
words.en: Unable to see; lacking the sense of sight.

words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.ex: The rich pay disproportionately more taxes.
words.ex_cn: 富人缴纳的税不成比例地更多。
words.en: To an extent that is too large or too small in comparison with something else.

words.ex: The company's turnaround came after new management took over.
words.ex_cn: 公司在新管理层接手后发生了转变。
words.en: A turnaround is a complete change in a situation or in the way that someone behaves.

words.tr: adj. 空气动力学的；流线型的
words.ex: The car has an aerodynamic shape to reduce wind resistance.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车具有流线型设计以减少风阻。
words.en: Relating to the science of the motion of air and other gases, and of the effects of such motion on objects in the flow.

words.ex: I checked the class schedule for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我查看了明天的课程时间表。
words.en: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

words.ex: The train's destination is Beijing.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车的目的地是北京。
words.en: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

words.ex: The plane landed on the runway.
words.ex_cn: 飞机降落在跑道上。
words.en: A runway is a strip of land where aircraft take off and land.

words.tr:
n. 陶瓷制品；陶瓷器；
adj. 陶质的；制陶的；
words.ex: He bought a ceramic bowl at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个陶瓷碗。
words.en: Ceramic is a hard material that is made by baking clay or similar substances at high temperatures. It is used to make things such as tiles, dishes, and statues.

words.ex: The glass broke into small fragments.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃碎成了小碎片。
words.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it.

words.tr: adj. 全音阶的；自然音阶的
words.ex: The piano plays a diatonic scale.
words.ex_cn: 钢琴弹奏了一个自然音阶。
words.en: Relating to a musical scale that comprises five whole tones and two semitones, making up the notes of the major or minor scale.

words.ex: The skeletal system supports the body.
words.ex_cn: 骨骼系统支撑身体。
words.en: Relating to, or forming a skeleton; very thin or emaciated.

words.ex: The company decided to outsource its customer service.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司决定将客户服务外购。
words.en: If a company outsources work or things, it pays workers from outside the company to do the work or supply the things.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The company updated the payroll last Friday.
words.ex_cn: 公司上星期五更新了职工工资册。
words.en: A payroll is a list of employees and the amount of money they are to be paid, or the total amount of money paid to the employees of a company.

words.ex: The deterioration of the road made driving dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 道路的恶化使驾驶变得危险。
words.en: The process of becoming progressively worse.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: He used 'she' as a pronoun in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他在句子中用'she'作为代词。
words.en: A pronoun is a word that is used instead of a noun or noun phrase. Pronouns refer to either a noun that has already been mentioned or to a noun that does not need to be named specifically.

words.tr: adj. 单个的；单数的；特异的；
words.ex: Each singular student must submit a form.
words.ex_cn: 每个学生都必须提交一份表格。
words.en: In grammar, singular means relating to or being a form of a word that refers to one person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 复数的； n. 复数；
words.ex: The word 'cats' is a plural form.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'cats' 是复数形式。
words.en: The plural form of a word is the form that is used when referring to more than one person or thing.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.ex: He has diabetes and must check his blood every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有糖尿病，必须每天检查血糖。
words.en: A medical condition in which the body cannot produce enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, leading to high levels of sugar in the blood.

words.ex: Each ommatidium in the fly's eye captures a small part of the image.
words.ex_cn: 苍蝇眼睛中的每个小眼单位捕捉图像的一小部分。
words.en: An ommatidium is one of the small optical units that make up the compound eye of an insect, each functioning as a separate visual receptor.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians built pyramids for their kings.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人为他们的国王建造了金字塔。
words.en: A pyramid is a monumental structure with a square or triangular base and sloping sides that meet in a point at the top, especially one built of stone as a royal tomb in ancient Egypt.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.tr: v. 结晶；定形；（使）具体化；变明确
words.ex: The idea began to crystallize after many talks.
words.ex_cn: 经过多次讨论，这个想法开始明朗起来。
words.en: To crystallize means to cause something to form into crystals or to become clear and definite in form.

words.ex: The soil has too much moisture.
words.ex_cn: 土壤中有太多湿气。
words.en: Moisture is tiny drops of water in the air, on a surface, or in a substance, that make it feel wet.

words.ex: He shows idolization for his favorite singer.
words.ex_cn: 他对最喜欢的歌手充满崇拜。
words.en: The act of admiring or loving someone or something very much, often too much.

words.ex: He shows veneration for his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他对祖父表示敬仰。
words.en: Veneration is a feeling of great respect or awe for someone or something.

words.ex: The lion is a carnivorous animal.
words.ex_cn: 狮子是一种食肉动物。
words.en: Carnivorous animals or plants eat meat.

words.ex: A dog is a mammal.
words.ex_cn: 狗是一种哺乳动物。
words.en: A mammal is a type of animal that feeds its young with milk produced by the mother's body. Mammals are warm-blooded and usually have hair or fur.

words.ex: The company made a cutback on office supplies.
words.ex_cn: 公司减少了办公用品的开支。
words.en: A reduction in something, especially in the amount of money spent on a particular thing.

words.ex: The music accompanies the dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐伴随舞蹈。
words.en: To go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to play a musical accompaniment for.

words.ex: He was a pioneer in space exploration.
words.ex_cn: 他是太空探索的先驱者。
words.en: A pioneer is someone who is one of the first people to do something that others will later develop or continue. Pioneers are also people who are among the first to go to live in a new area, especially in the past when people were trying to settle in new lands.

words.tr: n. 四分之一；季度；一刻钟；地区；方向；
words.ex: He ate a quarter of the pizza.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了四分之一的比萨。
words.en: A quarter is one of four equal parts of something, or a period of three months.

words.ex: This food contains a harmless additive for flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物含有用于调味的无害添加物。
words.en: An additive is a substance which is added in small amounts to something else in order to improve it, preserve it, or make it more effective.

words.tr: n. 易洛魁人（北美印第安人）；易洛魁语
words.ex: The Iroquois lived in longhouses in North America.
words.ex_cn: 易洛魁人住在北美的长屋里。
words.en: The Iroquois are a historically powerful northeast Native American confederacy.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.tr: n. 腰果（等于 cashew nut）；腰果树; adj. 漆树科的
words.ex: He eats a cashew every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一颗腰果。
words.en: A cashew is a kidney-shaped nut that grows at the end of the cashew apple, which is the fruit of the cashew tree, native to northeastern Brazil.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The dogs outnumber the cats in this neighborhood.
words.ex_cn: 这个社区里的狗比猫多。
words.en: If one group of people or things outnumbers another, the first group has more people or things in it than the second group.

words.ex: The paleontologist found a dinosaur bone in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 古生物学家在沙漠中发现了一块恐龙骨头。
words.en: A paleontologist is a scientist who studies fossils to understand the history of life on Earth.

words.ex: Monkeys and apes are primates.
words.ex_cn: 猴子和猿类是灵长类动物。
words.en: A primate is a member of the most developed and intelligent group of mammals, which includes humans, apes, and monkeys. In a religious context, a primate can also refer to the chief bishop or archbishop in a province or country.

words.ex: The boy has a chromosomal disorder.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩患有染色体疾病。
words.en: Relating to or involving chromosomes, which are structures within cells that contain DNA and protein.

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.tr: adj. 狭窄的； v. “cramp”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The tiny room was cramped and hard to move in.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间很狭窄，很难活动。
words.en: If a place is cramped, it is not big enough for the people or things in it, so that it is difficult to move around or to use things properly.

words.tr: n. 航空；航空学；飞行（术）；
words.ex: He works in aviation as a pilot.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一名飞行员从事航空工作。
words.en: Aviation is the operation and production of aircraft.

words.tr: n. 血吸虫病；裂体吸虫病；
words.ex: He got schistosomiasis from swimming in a dirty river.
words.ex_cn: 他因在脏河里游泳而感染了血吸虫病。
words.en: Schistosomiasis is a disease caused by infection with freshwater parasitic worms in certain tropical and subtropical countries.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr:
v. 下垂；下跌；消沉
n. 下垂；下跌；下陷
words.ex: The old bridge sags in the middle.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥中间下垂。
words.en: If something sags, it hangs down loosely or sinks downwards in the middle, often because it is not supported properly or because it is too heavy.

words.ex: He will pare the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他将用刀削苹果。
words.en: To pare something means to cut off its outer layer or to reduce its size or amount by cutting or trimming.

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.ex: He poured water into a wooden barrel.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进一个木桶里。
words.en: A barrel is a large, round container for liquids or food, typically made of wood or metal.

words.tr:
n. 预测；预报；
v. 预测；预报；
words.ex: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: If you forecast future events, you say what you think is going to happen in the future.

words.tr:
adj. 安坐的
v. 安置；使安顿；“ensconce”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was ensconced in his armchair with a book.
words.ex_cn: 他舒适地坐在扶手椅里看书。
words.en: To settle or establish someone or oneself in a comfortable, safe, or secret place.

words.tr: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；悲观的；
words.ex: He gave a cynical smile when they talked about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 当他们谈到诚实时，他露出了愤世嫉俗的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as cynical, you mean they believe that people always act selfishly.

words.tr: adj. 发光的；辐射的；容光焕发的
words.ex: The radiant sun warmed the garden.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的太阳温暖了花园。
words.en: If you describe someone as radiant, you mean that they look very happy and healthy.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: He meditates near the statue of Buddha.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在佛像附近冥想。
words.en: A Buddha is a person who has attained full enlightenment and has realized the ultimate truth.

words.tr: v. 置入神龛中；入庙祀奉；奉为神圣；珍藏
words.ex: They enshrined the ancient statue in a golden shrine.
words.ex_cn: 他们把这尊古代雕像置入了一个金色神龛中。
words.en: If something such as a tradition or a right is enshrined in something such as a constitution or law, it is protected by it.

words.tr:
v. 移居国外；把…逐出国外
n. 侨民；移居国外者
adj. 移居国外的；被逐出国外的
words.ex: He decided to expatriate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他决定移居加拿大以追求更好的生活。
words.en: An expatriate is someone who lives in a country that is not their own, often for work or political reasons.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: The ancient people worshipped a sun deity.
words.ex_cn: 古人崇拜太阳神。
words.en: A deity is a god or goddess, or anything revered as divine.

words.ex: The rock is made of schist.
words.ex_cn: 这种岩石由片岩组成。
words.en: Schist is a medium-grade metamorphic rock with medium to large, flat, sheet-like grains in a preferred orientation (nearby grains are roughly parallel).

words.ex: The book brought him great enlightenment.
words.ex_cn: 这本书给了他极大的启迪。
words.en: Enlightenment is the act of enlightening or the state of being enlightened. It can refer to the acquisition of spiritual knowledge or understanding, especially in Buddhism.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；好斗的；爱滋事的
words.ex: He is pugnacious and always argues with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他好斗，总是和同学争吵。
words.en: Someone who is pugnacious is eager to argue or fight.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.tr: n. 停战（协定）；休战（协定）
words.ex: The two sides agreed to a truce.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意停火。
words.en: A truce is an agreement between enemies or opponents to stop fighting or arguing for a certain time.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.tr: v. 重新集合；重新召集
words.ex: The committee will reconvene next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 委员会将在下周一重新召开。
words.en: To reconvene means to come together again after a break or to cause a group to come together again.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.ex: He has a predisposition to catch colds easily.
words.ex_cn: 他容易感冒的倾向。
words.en: A predisposition is a tendency to behave in a particular way or to suffer from a particular condition.

words.ex: The computer uses a buffer to store data temporarily.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用缓冲区临时存储数据。
words.en: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that reduces the impact of something.

words.ex: The breakwater protects the boat from big waves.
words.ex_cn: 防波堤保护船只免受大浪冲击。
words.en: A breakwater is a structure built to protect a harbor or shore from the force of waves.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.ex: The glacier moves slowly down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 冰川缓慢地沿着山向下移动。
words.en: A glacier is a large, persistent body of ice that forms where the accumulation of snow exceeds its ablation over many years, often centuries.

words.ex: The diamond is encased in glass.
words.ex_cn: 钻石被包裹在玻璃里。
words.en: To encase something means to cover or surround it completely in a case or close-fitting covering.

words.tr:
adj. 有生命的；有活力的
v. 使具活力；做成动画
words.ex: The cartoon characters are animate and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 这些卡通角色是有生命的，充满活力。
words.en: To animate something means to give it life or to make it lively and energetic.

words.ex: The earth's crust is made of rock.
words.ex_cn: 地球的地壳由岩石组成。
words.en: The crust is the hard outer layer of something, such as bread or the Earth's surface.

words.tr: adj. 无（接）缝的；无漏洞的；
words.ex: The software has a seamless interface.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件有一个无缝的界面。
words.en: Something that is seamless has no obvious joins or gaps between its different parts.

words.ex: The chair is stationary and does not move.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是固定的，不会移动。
words.en: not moving or not intended to be moved

words.ex: The colors of the painting fade in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的颜色在阳光下逐渐消失。
words.en: To gradually grow faint and disappear.

words.ex: The plant needs phosphate to grow well.
words.ex_cn: 植物需要磷酸盐才能良好生长。
words.en: A phosphate is a salt or ester of phosphoric acid, containing the anion PO₄³⁻ or the group —PO₄.

words.ex: The rhinoceros walks slowly in the grass.
words.ex_cn: 犀牛在草地上慢慢行走。
words.en: A rhinoceros is a large, thick-skinned animal with one or two horns on its nose, native to Africa and southern Asia.

words.ex: The poacher caught a tiger in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 偷猎者在森林里抓到了一只老虎。
words.en: A poacher is someone who hunts or catches animals illegally, especially on someone else's property.

words.ex: He loves reading literary books.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读文学书籍。
words.en: Literary means concerned with or connected with the writing, study, or appreciation of literature.

words.tr:
n. 抢救；
v. 打捞；挽救；抢救；
words.ex: The salvage of the ship took three days.
words.ex_cn: 对这艘船的抢救花了三天时间。
words.en: To salvage something means to retrieve or preserve it from loss or destruction, especially from a shipwreck or fire. It can also refer to the act of saving or rescuing something from a difficult situation.

words.ex: The sloth moves very slowly in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 树懒在树上移动得非常慢。
words.en: Sloth is a disinclination to work or exert oneself; laziness, or a slow-moving tropical American mammal that lives in trees.

words.ex: The baby ingests milk every few hours.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿每隔几小时喝奶。
words.en: To ingest means to take food, drink, or another substance into your body, usually by swallowing.

words.tr:
adj. 失职的；违法的；拖欠债务的
n. 违犯者；少年罪犯；违法者
words.ex: The delinquent worker ignored his duties.
words.ex_cn: 这位失职的员工忽视了他的职责。
words.en: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits a crime or breaks the law.

words.ex: The police caught the perpetrator of the robbery.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了抢劫案的作恶者。
words.en: A perpetrator is someone who has committed a crime or a morally wrong act.

words.ex: He has a lot of mucous in his nose.
words.ex_cn: 他的鼻子有很多黏液。
words.en: Relating to, producing, or resembling mucus.

words.ex: The house has a freestanding garage.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个独立式的车库。
words.en: A freestanding object or structure is one that is not attached to or supported by another structure.

words.ex: The ozone layer protects us from the sun's harmful rays.
words.ex_cn: 臭氧层保护我们免受太阳有害射线的伤害。
words.en: Ozone is a form of oxygen that has three atoms in each molecule, and it is a pale blue gas with a pungent smell. It is found in the Earth's atmosphere and absorbs ultraviolet radiation, which is harmful to living organisms.

words.ex: The car burns hydrocarbon fuel.
words.ex_cn: 汽车燃烧碳氢化合物燃料。
words.en: A hydrocarbon is an organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon.

words.ex: Plants need nitrogen to grow.
words.ex_cn: 植物需要氮来生长。
words.en: A chemical element with the symbol N and atomic number 7. It is a colorless, odorless, tasteless gas that is the most plentiful element in Earth's atmosphere and is a constituent of all living tissues.

words.ex: The factory releases a pollutant into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向河里排放一种污染物。
words.en: A pollutant is a substance that pollutes something, especially air, water, or soil.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.tr: v. 使开化；使文明；教化
words.ex: They tried to civilize the wild tribe.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图使这个原始部落文明化。
words.en: To civilize means to bring a place or people to a stage of social, cultural, and moral development considered to be more advanced.

words.ex: The vintner grows grapes and makes wine.
words.ex_cn: 这位酿酒师种植葡萄并酿造葡萄酒。
words.en: A vintner is a person who makes or sells wine.

words.ex: The theater's repertory includes classic plays and modern dramas.
words.ex_cn: 这家剧院的全部剧目包括经典戏剧和现代戏剧。
words.en: A repertory is a collection of pieces of music or plays that a company or performer knows or is prepared to perform.

words.ex: Pop music is part of the mainstream.
words.ex_cn: 流行音乐是主流的一部分。
words.en: The ideas, attitudes, or activities that are shared by most people and regarded as normal or conventional.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.ex: The study used a longitudinal design to track changes over time.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用了纵向设计来追踪随时间的变化。
words.en: Relating to the length of something rather than its width; extending in the direction of the length.

words.ex: The nail fits into the groove.
words.ex_cn: 钉子卡在槽里。
words.en: A groove is a long, narrow space or cut in a surface, often made to guide the movement of something or to hold something in place. It can also refer to a settled routine or way of doing things that is hard to change.

words.ex: The slow computer is a bottleneck in our work.
words.ex_cn: 这台慢电脑是我们工作的瓶颈。
words.en: A bottleneck is a point of congestion in a system that occurs when workloads arrive too quickly for the system to handle. In terms of traffic, it refers to a narrow section of road or a junction that impedes traffic flow.

words.ex: He is a famous playwright who writes plays.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的剧作家，写剧本。
words.en: A playwright is a person who writes plays.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.ex: A wasp flew into the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 一只黄蜂飞进了厨房。
words.en: A wasp is a flying insect that can sting people and is often yellow and black in color.

words.tr: adj. 不能生育的；贫瘠的；
words.ex: The doctor said the man is sterile.
words.ex_cn: 医生说这个人不能生育。
words.en: Something that is sterile is completely clean and free from bacteria or other microorganisms.

words.ex: He capitalized on the chance to start a business.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了这个创业的机会。
words.en: To capitalize means to use something to your advantage, especially in a way that brings financial gain. It can also mean to write or print a word with its first letter as a capital letter.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；热心的；敏锐的；
words.ex: He is keen to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望学习英语。
words.en: If you are keen on doing something, you very much want to do it. If you are keen that something should happen, you very much want it to happen.

words.tr:
n. 代用品；代替物；
v. 替代；
words.ex: Honey is a good substitute for sugar.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是糖的良好代用品。
words.en: A substitute is something or someone that takes the place or function of another.

words.ex: He majors in criminology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学主修犯罪学。
words.en: Criminology is the scientific study of crime and criminals.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.tr: adj. 放任的；纵容的；许可的
words.ex: Her parents are permissive and let her stay out late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很宽容，让她很晚才回家。
words.en: A permissive person, society, or system allows people a lot of freedom to do what they want.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.ex: They visited the Colosseum in Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了罗马的斗兽场。
words.en: The Colosseum is an oval amphitheatre in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy. Built of concrete and sand, it is the largest amphitheatre ever built.

words.tr: n. 露天历史剧；盛装游行（或庆典）；选美比赛
words.ex: The town held a pageant to show the history of the old kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇举办了一场露天历史剧，以展示古老王国的历史。
words.en: A pageant is a public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colorful costumes, or an outdoor performance of a historical scene.

words.ex: The fireworks at night were a beautiful spectacle.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的烟花是一场美丽的奇观。
words.en: A spectacle is a visually striking performance or display.

words.ex: The baby grows in the mother's womb.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿在母亲的子宫里成长。
words.en: The organ in the lower body of a woman or female mammal where offspring are conceived and in which they gestate before birth.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.ex: This plant has regenerative powers.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物具有再生能力。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by regeneration; able to regrow or be renewed.

words.tr: adj. 极小的；微小的；微量的；
words.ex: The tiny ant carried a big leaf.
words.ex_cn: 这只极小的蚂蚁搬着一片大叶子。
words.en: Very small in size or amount.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: He is an expert in the domain of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 他是人工智能领域的专家。
words.en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

words.ex: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: A catastrophic event or situation is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.tr:
v. 分开；分裂；
n. 划分；分歧；
words.ex: The tree split in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那棵树在风暴中裂开了。
words.en: If something splits or if you split it, it is divided into two or more parts.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: We visited an art gallery on Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 我们周日参观了一家艺术画廊。
words.en: A gallery is a place where works of art are shown to the public.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: The king sat on the throne.
words.ex_cn: 国王坐在王位上。
words.en: The throne is the special chair used by a king, queen, or emperor during ceremonies, or the position of being a ruler.

words.ex: The sun descends behind the hills.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在山后落下。
words.en: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.

words.tr: adj. 水生的；水栖的；水中的；
words.ex: The fish live in aquatic plants.
words.ex_cn: 这些鱼生活在水生植物中。
words.en: Relating to water; living in or near water or taking place in water.

words.tr:
n. （潜水艇或潜水者的）通气管
v. 戴潜水通气管潜泳
words.ex: He put on his mask and snorkel to swim over the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 他戴上口罩和通气管，在珊瑚礁上游泳。
words.en: A snorkel is a tube that allows a swimmer to breathe while floating face down on the surface of the water.

words.tr: n. 精神变态者；变态人格者
words.ex: The psychopath was diagnosed with antisocial personality disorder.
words.ex_cn: 这名精神病患者被诊断为反社会人格障碍。
words.en: A psychopath is someone who has a serious mental illness that causes them to behave in a violent or criminal way without feeling guilty.

words.ex: She showed compassion for the homeless man.
words.ex_cn: 她对那个无家可归的人表示同情。
words.en: Compassion is a feeling of pity, sympathy, and understanding for someone who is suffering.

words.ex: He listened to his conscience and told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他听从了良心，说出了真相。
words.en: Your conscience is the part of your mind that tells you whether what you are doing is right or wrong.

words.tr: adj. 开胃的；促进食欲的
words.ex: The smell of the food was appetizing.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味很诱人。
words.en: If you describe food as appetizing, you mean that it looks or smells good and makes you want to eat it.

words.ex: My grandmother gave me the heirloom necklace.
words.ex_cn: 奶奶把这串祖传的项链给了我。
words.en: An heirloom is a valuable object that has belonged to a family for several generations.

words.ex: There was a resurgence of interest in classical music last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年古典音乐的兴趣再次兴起。
words.en: A resurgence is a process in which something becomes active or popular again after a period of inactivity or unpopularity.

words.ex: He completed his apprenticeship as a carpenter.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了木工学徒期。
words.en: An apprenticeship is a period of time in which someone learns a trade or profession by working under the supervision of a skilled worker.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.ex: The story had a graphic description of the battle.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事对战斗的描述非常生动。
words.en: A graphic is a visual representation of data or information, such as a chart, diagram, or picture.

words.tr: adj. 数值的；数字的（等于 numerical）; n. 数；数字
words.ex: The code uses numeric values to calculate the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个代码使用数值来计算结果。
words.en: Numeric means relating to numbers or consisting of numbers.

words.ex: The study uses quantitative data to measure results.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用定量数据来测量结果。
words.en: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality.

words.ex: The teacher drew a diagram to explain the water cycle.
words.ex_cn: 老师画了一个图表来解释水循环。
words.en: A diagram is a simple drawing which consists mainly of lines and is used, for example, to explain how a machine works.

words.tr: adj. [数] 代数的；关于代数学的
words.ex: He solved the algebraic equation quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解出了这个代数方程。
words.en: Relating to or involving algebra.

words.ex: He uses a spreadsheet to count his money.
words.ex_cn: 他用电子表格来计算他的钱。
words.en: A spreadsheet is a computer program that is used for displaying and dealing with numbers. It shows numbers in rows and columns, and it is used especially for doing financial calculations and for creating graphs.

words.tr: n. 进入；入口；条目；参与；参赛作品；
words.ex: The entry to the building is locked after 10 PM.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物在晚上10点后进入通道会被锁上。
words.en: An entry is the act of going into a place or the right to go into it. It can also refer to a door, gate, or passage by which you enter a place. Additionally, an entry can be a piece of information recorded in a book, list, or computer, or the act of recording it.

words.tr: n. 测量仪器；规格；评估；
words.ex: The mechanic used a gauge to check the tire pressure.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用一个测量仪器来检查轮胎气压。
words.en: A gauge is a device that measures the amount or quantity of something and shows the measurement in a form that is easy to read, such as a dial or a digital display.

words.ex: He adds sweetener to his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他往咖啡里加甜味剂。
words.en: A sweetener is a substance used to sweeten food or drink, especially one that does not contain sugar.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏兴趣的；漠不关心的；
words.ex: He was apathetic about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影缺乏兴趣。
words.en: If you describe someone as apathetic, you are criticizing them because they do not seem to be interested in or enthusiastic about doing anything.

words.ex: He became a dropout after failing math class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试不及格后退学了。
words.en: A dropout is a person who leaves school or college before they have finished their studies, especially because they are not interested in continuing.

words.tr: n. 总部；司令部；指挥部；
words.ex: The company's headquarters is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: The main office or center of control of a company, organization, or military unit.

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.ex: He reads books in his leisure.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.ex: He gave a generous donation to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨地捐钱给穷人。
words.en: A generous person gives more of something, especially money, than is usual or expected.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: The car has a sleek design.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有着流畅的外形。
words.en: Sleek describes something that is smooth, glossy, and streamlined, often implying a sense of elegance and efficiency.

words.tr: adj. 压倒的；无法抗拒的；势不可挡的； v. “overwhelm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The crowd's cheers were overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 人群的欢呼声压倒了一切。
words.en: If something is overwhelming, it affects you very strongly, and you do not know how to deal with it.

words.ex: He works at a small pharmacy near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园附近的一家小药房工作。
words.en: A pharmacy is a shop or a department in a shop where medicines are prepared and sold.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.ex: He wears a badge on his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他衬衫上戴着一枚徽章。
words.en: A badge is a small piece of metal, plastic, or cloth which you wear in order to show people that you have a particular rank, job, or belong to a particular group.

words.ex: They celebrated their wedding anniversary with dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们用晚餐庆祝结婚纪念日。
words.en: An anniversary is a date which is remembered or celebrated because a special event happened on that date in a previous year.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: The doctor checked his daily intake of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他每天的糖摄入量。
words.en: The process of taking something in, especially food, air, or information.

words.tr:
n. 素食者；食草动物；
adj. 素食者的；素菜的；
words.ex: He is a vegetarian and doesn't eat meat.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名素食者，不吃肉。
words.en: A vegetarian is someone who does not eat meat or fish, and sometimes other animal products, especially for moral, religious, or health reasons.

words.ex: He was arrested for vagrancy after sleeping on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他因在街上睡觉而因流浪罪被捕。
words.en: The state or condition of wandering from place to place without a home or job.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.tr: n. 优惠券；息票；配给券
words.ex: He used a coupon to buy milk at half price.
words.ex_cn: 他用一张优惠券以半价买了牛奶。
words.en: A coupon is a piece of printed paper that allows you to pay less money than usual for a product, or to get it free.

words.ex: The ad is on a big billboard near the road.
words.ex_cn: 广告牌在路边的大广告牌上。
words.en: A billboard is a large outdoor board for displaying advertisements.

words.ex: The company will reallocate funds to the marketing team.
words.ex_cn: 公司将把资金重新分配给市场团队。
words.en: To allocate (resources or duties) again or differently.

words.ex: He wrote a memorandum about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份关于会议的备忘录。
words.en: A memorandum is a written proposal or reminder, especially in a business context.

words.ex: Obesity is a serious health problem in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 肥胖是许多国家的一个严重健康问题。
words.en: Obesity is a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated to the extent that it may have a negative effect on health.

words.ex: He stayed in a deluxe room at the hotel.
words.ex_cn: 他住在酒店的豪华房间里。
words.en: If you describe something as deluxe, you mean that it is very luxurious and expensive.

words.tr: n. 洗发水；洗发精；洗发香波；
words.ex: She bought a new shampoo at the store.
words.ex_cn: 她在商店买了一瓶新的洗发水。
words.en: Shampoo is a liquid soap that is used for washing your hair, or the act of washing your hair with this liquid.

words.tr: n. 恣意毁坏他人财产罪
words.ex: The boys did vandalism by breaking the windows.
words.ex_cn: 那些男孩通过砸坏窗户实施了破坏行为。
words.en: The crime of deliberately damaging or destroying public or private property.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.ex: The movie had a sequel that came out last year.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一部去年上映的续集。
words.en: A sequel is a book, film, or play that continues the story of a previous one.

words.tr: n. 垃圾填埋（场）；垃圾堆填（区）；
words.ex: The city built a new landfill outside the town.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市在城外建了一个新的垃圾填埋场。
words.en: A landfill is a place where waste is buried under the ground.

words.ex: The poll showed that most people support the new law.
words.ex_cn: 这项民意调查表明，大多数人支持这项新法律。
words.en: A poll is a survey in which people are asked their opinions about something, usually in order to find out how popular something is or what people intend to do in the future.

words.tr:
v. 进行无记名投票 
n. 无记名投票
words.ex: He cast his ballot in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中投了票。
words.en: A ballot is a process of voting, in writing and typically in secret. It is also the piece of paper on which you mark your vote.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.ex: The school invited its alumni to the annual reunion.
words.ex_cn: 学校邀请了它的校友参加年度聚会。
words.en: Alumni are former students of a particular school, college, or university.

words.ex: The donor gave money to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 捐赠者向医院捐了钱。
words.en: A donor is a person or organization that gives something, especially money, to a charity or other organization.

words.tr:
v. 酿造；沏；酝酿
n. 酿造的饮料；啤酒
words.ex: He brews coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冲咖啡。
words.en: If you brew tea or coffee, you make it by pouring hot water over tea leaves or ground coffee. If you brew beer, you make it by soaking grain in water and then fermenting it.

words.tr: n. 客厅；起居室；营业室
words.ex: They sat in the parlor and drank tea.
words.ex_cn: 他们坐在客厅里喝茶。
words.en: A parlor is a room in a house for the special use of visitors, or a room in a public building for a specific purpose.

words.tr: adj. 迟的；缓慢的；迟缓的
words.ex: He is tardy for school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上学都迟到。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tardy, you think that they are later than they should be or later than expected.

words.ex: He plays the accordion at the street festival.
words.ex_cn: 他在街头音乐节上演奏手风琴。
words.en: An accordion is a musical instrument that you play by pressing keys or buttons on one side and pulling and pushing a bellows on the other side to force air through reeds, producing notes.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.tr:
adj. 粉状的；涂粉的
v. 搽粉于； 撒粉；使成粉末；“powder”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He added powdered sugar to the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他往咖啡里加了糖粉。
words.en: Made into or resembling powder.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.ex: They erect a flagpole in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们在公园里竖立一根旗杆。
words.en: If people erect something such as a building, bridge, or barrier, they build it or create it.

words.ex: The water in the pond was stagnant.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里的水不流动。
words.en: If something such as a business or economy is stagnant, there is little activity or change.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.ex: The therapeutic massage helped her relax.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗性的按摩帮助她放松了。
words.en: If something is therapeutic, it helps you to relax or to feel better about things, especially if you have been feeling worried or upset.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.ex: The teacher gave me feedback on my essay.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我关于我作文的反馈。
words.en: Feedback is comments in the form of opinions about and reactions to something, intended to provide useful information for future decisions and development.

words.tr: v. 发音；宣告；“pronounce”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 显著的；
words.ex: He pronounced the word correctly.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地发音了这个单词。
words.en: Something that is pronounced is very noticeable or obvious.

words.ex: The doctor checked his intestinal health.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠道健康。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the intestines.

words.ex: He chose an occupational therapy course.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了一门职业治疗课程。
words.en: Relating to a job or profession.

words.ex: He gave an enumeration of all the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他列出了书架上所有的书。
words.en: The act of naming things one by one or a list of items.

words.tr:
n. 家庭；
adj. 家庭的；
words.ex: This household has three children.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭有三个孩子。
words.en: A household is all the people in a family or group who live together in a house.

words.ex: The school has a hierarchical system.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个等级制度。
words.en: A hierarchical system or organization is one in which people have different ranks or positions, depending on how important they are.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.tr: adj. 有声望的；声誉好的
words.ex: He works for a reputable company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家信誉良好的公司工作。
words.en: A reputable person or organization is considered to be good and trustworthy by most people.

words.tr: adv. 任意地; 武断地
words.ex: He chose the number arbitrarily.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地选了这个数字。
words.en: If something is done arbitrarily, it is done without any reason or system, often in a way that is unfair.

words.tr:
n. 问题；重要议题；发行（物）；
v. 发行；
words.ex: The main issue is lack of money.
words.ex_cn: 主要问题是缺乏资金。
words.en: An issue is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or arguing about.

words.ex: The statistician analyzed the survey data.
words.ex_cn: 这位统计学家分析了调查数据。
words.en: A statistician is a person who specializes in the study and interpretation of numerical data, especially in order to make predictions or inferences about a population or a process.

words.tr:
n. 新闻界；出版社；
v. 按；压；
words.ex: The press reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: To press something is to push it firmly, often with your fingers or hand, in order to operate a device or machine, or to make something flat or smooth. It can also mean to urge someone to do something or to make a strong demand for something.

words.tr: adj. 彻底的；完全的；详尽的；
words.ex: He did a thorough cleaning of the house.
words.ex_cn: 他对房子进行了彻底的清洁。
words.en: A thorough action or activity is one that is done very carefully and in a detailed way so that nothing is forgotten.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

words.ex: There was a controversy about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 关于新校规，人们展开了争论。
words.en: A controversy is a disagreement or argument about something that involves many people and generates strong feelings.

words.ex: The density of water is 1 gram per cubic centimeter.
words.ex_cn: 水的密度是每立方厘米1克。
words.en: Density is a measure of how much mass is contained in a given unit volume of a substance.

words.tr:
n. 企图；试图；
v. 企图；试图；
words.ex: His attempt to cheat on the test failed.
words.ex_cn: 他企图在考试中作弊，但失败了。
words.en: To make an effort to achieve or complete something, especially something difficult.

words.ex: The door opens on a metal hinge.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门装在一个金属枢纽上。
words.en: A hinge is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is used to join two things together so that one of them can swing or move freely.

words.tr: n. 合法化；承认为嫡出
words.ex: The law gave legitimation to the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 法律给予了这项新政策合法性。
words.en: The act of making something legal or legitimate.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.tr:
n. 安逸；轻松；
v. 缓解；减轻；
words.ex: He enjoys the ease of living in a quiet village.
words.ex_cn: 他享受住在安静村庄里的安逸。
words.en: If you talk about the ease of a particular activity, you are referring to the way that it has been made easier to do, or to the fact that it is already easy to do. Ease is also a state of being comfortable and without worry or anxiety.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.ex: They maintain correspondence through letters.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过信件保持通信联系。
words.en: Communication by exchanging letters with someone; a close similarity, connection, or equivalence.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: The police will investigate the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方将调查这起事故。
words.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

words.ex: The supreme leader makes the final decision.
words.ex_cn: 至上的领导人做出最终决定。
words.en: If you say that something is supreme, you mean that it is the most important or the best of its kind.

words.ex: The country made a unilateral decision to close the border.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家单方面决定关闭边境。
words.en: Involving only one group or country.

words.tr: adj. 深远的；影响深远的
words.ex: The decision had far-reaching effects on the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对这个城镇产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe actions, events, or changes as far-reaching, you mean that they have a very great influence and affect a great number of things.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.tr: n. 房间；室；腔；大会议室；
words.ex: He sat in the chamber and waited quietly.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在房间里安静地等待。
words.en: A chamber is a large room, especially one that is used for formal or public events.

words.ex: The ratification of the treaty took two years.
words.ex_cn: 该条约的批准花了两年时间。
words.en: The act of giving formal consent to a treaty, contract, or agreement, making it officially valid.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: The scientist debunked the myth that sugar makes children hyper.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家揭穿了糖会使孩子多动的谬论。
words.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is.

words.ex: He is a revisionist historian who questions old stories.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位修正主义历史学家，质疑旧的故事。
words.en: A revisionist is someone who advocates or practices revision, especially of a political or historical nature, often challenging the accepted views or interpretations.

words.tr:
n. 上升；提高；
v. 上升；提高；
words.ex: There was a rise in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度上升了。
words.en: If an amount or level rises, it increases; if something rises, it moves upwards; if you rise, you stand up; if you rise, you get out of bed.

words.ex: The two countries formed an alliance to fight the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成联盟以对抗敌人。
words.en: An alliance is a group of countries or political parties that are formally united and working together because they have similar aims.

words.ex: The demise of the old king shocked the nation.
words.ex_cn: 老国王的去世震惊了全国。
words.en: The demise of something or someone is their end or death.

words.ex: The painter portrays a happy family in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这位画家在画中描绘了一个幸福的家庭。
words.en: To portray someone or something means to show or represent them in a painting, film, book, or other artistic work.

words.tr: adj. 有特权的； v. “privilege”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a privileged student who gets free books.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有特权的学生，能免费获得书籍。
words.en: Having special rights, advantages, or immunities.

words.tr: adj. 不矛盾的；可和解的；可调和的
words.ex: Their differences are reconcilable and can be resolved through dialogue.
words.ex_cn: 他们的分歧是可以调和的，可以通过对话解决。
words.en: Capable of being reconciled; able to be made compatible or consistent.

words.tr: adj. [数] 可约的，可化简的；可还原的；可缩小的
words.ex: This fraction is reducible to a simpler form.
words.ex_cn: 这个分数可以化简为更简单的形式。
words.en: Capable of being reduced or simplified.

words.tr: adj. 包容的；包含全部费用的；
words.ex: The school is inclusive and welcomes all students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校是包容的，欢迎所有学生。
words.en: Inclusive is used to describe something that is designed to include all types of people, things, or ideas, and to treat them all fairly and equally.

words.tr: v. 使根深蒂固；使处于牢固地位；用壕沟围住
words.ex: The habit entrenches itself over time.
words.ex_cn: 这个习惯随着时间的推移变得根深蒂固。
words.en: To establish something very firmly so that it is very difficult to change.

words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.ex: The company is improving its recruitment process.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司正在改进它的招聘流程。
words.en: The process of finding and hiring new employees for a company or organization.

words.ex: The emancipation of slaves ended centuries of oppression.
words.ex_cn: 奴隶的解放结束了几个世纪的压迫。
words.en: The act of freeing someone from legal, social, or political restrictions.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: She combines flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To combine means to join or merge two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.ex: Each participant must sign the form.
words.ex_cn: 每个参与者都必须签署表格。
words.en: A participant is someone who takes part in an activity or event.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: The teacher gave precedence to students who arrived early.
words.ex_cn: 老师给早到的学生优先权。
words.en: If one thing takes precedence over another, it is regarded as more important than the other thing and is dealt with first.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.tr:
n. 母亲身份；
adj. 产妇的；
words.ex: She enjoys her maternity after giving birth to her first child.
words.ex_cn: 她在生下第一个孩子后享受做母亲的身份。
words.en: Maternity refers to the state of being a mother or the period during which a woman is pregnant or has recently given birth.

words.ex: He took an intensive English course last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他参加了一个密集的英语课程。
words.en: Intensive is used to describe something that involves a lot of effort, energy, or attention in a short period of time.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的；有说服力的； v. 说服；“convince”的现在分词；
words.ex: His argument was convincing.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点令人信服。
words.en: A convincing argument, evidence, or person is one that makes you believe that something is true or right.

words.ex: The houses are sparsely spread across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 房子稀疏地分布在沙漠中。
words.en: In a sparse manner; not densely or thickly.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: The company's paternalistic policies included providing housing for its employees.
words.ex_cn: 公司的家长式政策包括为员工提供住房。
words.en: If you describe a person or organization as paternalistic, you mean that they act in a way that is like a father looking after his children, especially by controlling them without giving them any responsibility or freedom.

words.tr: adj. 扭曲的； v. “distort”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The mirror made her face look distorted.
words.ex_cn: 镜子让她的脸看起来扭曲了。
words.en: If something is distorted, it has been changed from its usual, original, natural, or intended meaning, condition, or shape.

words.tr: adj. 放纵的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: His intemperate lifestyle led to numerous health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他放纵的生活方式导致了许多健康问题。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or behaviour as intemperate, you are critical of them because they are too extreme and uncontrolled.

words.ex: His argument is based on a fallacy.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点基于一个谬误。
words.en: A fallacy is an idea which many people believe to be true, but which is in fact false because it is based on incorrect information or reasoning.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.tr: n. （为军队或其他组织的）采购
words.ex: The army's procurement of food and fuel takes months.
words.ex_cn: 军队的食品和燃料采购需要数月时间。
words.en: Procurement is the act of obtaining or buying goods and services, often for a business or government.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: He explicitly said no to the offer.
words.ex_cn: 他明确地拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: In a clear and detailed manner, leaving no room for confusion or doubt.

words.tr: v. 证明...正当；“justify”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 有正当理由的；
words.ex: He justified his actions by telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他通过讲真话来证明自己的行为是正当的。
words.en: If you describe a decision, action, or idea as justified, you think it is reasonable and acceptable because it is based on facts or good reasons.

words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr: n. 对应物；相当之物；副本；
words.ex: The CEO's counterpart in China signed the agreement.
words.ex_cn: 中国方面的对应人物签署了协议。
words.en: Someone's or something's counterpart is another person or thing that has a similar function or position in a different place.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: His preeminence in the field of medicine is undisputed.
words.ex_cn: 他在医学领域的卓越地位是毋庸置疑的。
words.en: The state of being superior to all others in status, quality, or importance.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 品行端正的；品德高的；
words.ex: He is a virtuous man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品行端正的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Having or showing high moral standards.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.tr: v. 承诺；犯（罪、错）；（公开地）表达意见；
words.ex: He commit to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺帮助他的朋友。
words.en: To commit means to carry out or perpetrate a mistake, crime, or immoral act; or to pledge or bind oneself to a certain course of action.

words.tr: adv. 密切地；亲密地；谙熟地；
words.ex: They are intimately connected by family ties.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过家庭关系密切相连。
words.en: In a way that involves a close link or relationship; closely.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显著的； v. 打击；“strike”的现在分词；
words.ex: The painting has a striking color scheme.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有着引人注目的配色。
words.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.ex: The concert was the culmination of his music career.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会是他音乐生涯的顶点。
words.en: The culmination of something is the highest or final point of it, often after a long period of development.

words.tr:
v. 使腐败；
adj. 腐败的；
words.ex: The official was corrupt by taking bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员因收受贿赂而腐败。
words.en: If someone is corrupt, they do things that are dishonest or illegal in order to gain money or power.

words.tr: n. 物物交换；实物交易；
words.ex: They used barter to trade apples for eggs.
words.ex_cn: 他们用物物交换的方式用苹果换鸡蛋。
words.en: To trade goods or services without using money.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.tr: adj. 随后的；后来的；接踵而至的； v. “ensue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ensuing meeting was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 随后的会议被取消了。
words.en: Following immediately after something else.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: He seeks help when he is stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当他遇到困难时，他会寻求帮助。
words.en: If you seek something, you try to find it or obtain it.

words.ex: I anticipate rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我预料明天会下雨。
words.en: If you anticipate an event, you realize in advance that it may happen and you are prepared for it.

words.ex: He gave a reasonable answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个合理的回答。
words.en: Fair and sensible; not excessive or extreme.

words.tr: adv. 公认地；普遍承认地；诚然；
words.ex: Admittedly, he is not the best player, but he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 公认地，他不是最好的球员，但他很努力。
words.en: Used to express that you accept something is true or that you agree with it, even though you may not like it.

words.ex: The road inclines sharply to the top of the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这条路陡峭地倾斜向山顶。
words.en: If you incline to a particular opinion, you have a tendency to think or behave in a particular way.

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.ex: His ignorance of the rules caused the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的无知导致了这个错误。
words.en: Lack of knowledge or information.

words.ex: Try to lessen your sugar intake.
words.ex_cn: 试着减少你的糖摄入量。
words.en: If something lessens or you lessen it, it becomes smaller in size, amount, degree, or importance.

words.ex: The professionalization of teaching has improved school quality.
words.ex_cn: 教学的职业化提高了学校质量。
words.en: The process of becoming professional or the state of being professional, especially in a particular field of activity.

words.ex: This movie is a horror genre film.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部恐怖类型影片。
words.en: A genre is a particular type of literature, painting, music, film, or other art form which people consider as a class because it has special characteristics.

words.ex: It's an irony that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: Irony is a subtle form of humor which involves saying things that you do not mean.

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.tr: adj. 档案的；关于档案的
words.ex: The archival documents provide valuable insights into the past.
words.ex_cn: 这些档案文件为过去提供了宝贵的见解。
words.en: Relating to or contained in archives.

words.ex: The framework of the house is made of wood.
words.ex_cn: 房子的骨架是木制的。
words.en: A framework is a particular set of rules, ideas, or beliefs which you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do.

words.ex: He wrote a memoir about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一本关于自己童年的回忆录。
words.en: A memoir is a book or article that you write about someone who you have known, describing what you remember of them and of particular events in which you both took part.

words.ex: The scandal brought the company into disrepute.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻使该公司声名狼藉。
words.en: If someone or something is in disrepute, they have a bad reputation because people think they have done something bad or wrong.

words.tr:
n. 业余爱好者；
adj. 业余的；
words.ex: He is an amateur who paints on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他是个周末画画的业余爱好者。
words.en: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.tr: adj. 可比较的；比得上的；类似的；
words.ex: The prices of these two phones are comparable.
words.ex_cn: 这两部手机的价格是可比较的。
words.en: Something that is comparable to something else is similar in size, amount, or quality.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.ex: He is aware of the danger.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到危险。
words.en: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

words.ex: The court followed the precedent set in 1995.
words.ex_cn: 法院遵循了1995年确立的先例。
words.en: A precedent is an action or decision that is used as an example when someone wants to do a similar thing in the future.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的减价票。
words.en: A concession is a point or principle that is granted or acknowledged in the course of an argument or negotiation, often as a compromise or to facilitate agreement.

words.ex: He made an adjustment to live in the new city.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了适应以适应新城市的生活。
words.en: An adjustment is a small change that is made to something such as a machine or a way of doing something.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.tr: v. 察觉；“perceive”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He perceived a change in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他察觉到她的声音有了变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.tr:
n. 诉讼当事人
adj. 有关诉讼的
words.ex: The litigant spoke clearly in court.
words.ex_cn: 这位诉讼当事人在法庭上清晰地发言。
words.en: A litigant is a person who is involved in a lawsuit.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.ex: The premise of his argument is that everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他论点的前提是人人平等。
words.en: A premise is a statement or idea that forms the basis for a reasonable line of argument.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.ex: The outcome of the game was a tie.
words.ex_cn: 比赛的结果是平局。
words.en: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

words.ex: The mechanic fixed my car quickly.
words.ex_cn: 机修工很快修好了我的车。
words.en: A mechanic is a person whose job is to repair and maintain machines and engines, especially those of vehicles.

words.tr:
n. 决策人；行政官；管理人员；
adj. 行政的；决策的；
words.ex: The executive decided to launch the new product.
words.ex_cn: 这位决策人决定推出新产品。
words.en: An executive is a person who has a senior management position in a business or other organization.

words.tr: n. 估价员；（资产）评估师；评分者
words.ex: The assessor evaluated the property's value for tax purposes.
words.ex_cn: 评估员为征税目的评估了房产的价值。
words.en: An assessor is a person whose job is to calculate the value of something or the amount of money that should be paid, for example in tax.

words.ex: The chemicals are hazardous to health.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质对健康有危险。
words.en: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

words.tr: adj. 可扣除的；可减免的
words.ex: The insurance plan has a deductible fee.
words.ex_cn: 这个保险计划有一个可扣除的费用。
words.en: In insurance, the deductible is the amount of money that you have to pay before the insurance company will pay any expenses.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: He went to the clinic for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去诊所做检查。
words.en: A clinic is a place where people receive medical treatment or advice, especially for a particular illness or condition.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.ex: A car has many components, like wheels and engines.
words.ex_cn: 汽车有许多部分，比如轮子和发动机。
words.en: A component is a part of a larger whole, especially a part that can be separated from or attached to a system.

words.tr: phrase. 覆盖范围的文字说明；用于描述某项服务或产品覆盖区域的标注文字
words.ex: The map includes a coverage lettering that explains the service areas.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图包含了一段文字说明，解释了服务范围。
words.en: Text or lettering used to describe or provide information about an insurance policy's coverage.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is a preventive measure.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔是一种预防性的措施。
words.en: Designed to stop something undesirable from occurring.
